title: PromptTestEnv benchmark report
description: The file written by `prompttestenv run --output-mode json` (or `render --output-mode json`) under a project's Report/ directory. It carries the same content as the HTML report, plus the per-repetition raw values the page reduces to mean and standard deviation. SENTINEL: throughout this document, -1 means 'not measured' — a judge call that failed, a metric that was switched off, or a quantity with nothing to compute it from. It is never a low measurement. Where a field says so explicitly, 0.0 is instead a real measurement and must not be conflated with -1. The responses of repetitions other than the best-scoring one are not here; they live in the project's progress.jsonl.

schema_version.description: Version of this report format. Bumped when the payload shape changes.

generated_at.description: Local time the file was written, ISO 8601 to the second. This is when the report was rendered, not when the benchmark ran: a `render` re-issues it against an older progress.jsonl.

project_name.description: Basename of the benchmark project directory.

verdict.description: The comparative conclusion written by the verdict judge. When the project sets group_verdicts, the judge writes one verdict per test-case group plus a synthesis; otherwise there is a single verdict and `groups` is empty.

grouped.description: True when the verdict is split per group.

groups.description: Per-group verdicts, empty when `grouped` is false.

group_name.description: The `group` field shared by the test cases this verdict covers.

verdict.description: Markdown body of this group's verdict.

global_verdict.description: The overall conclusion, as Markdown. When `grouped` is false this is the whole verdict.

text.description: The verdict exactly as stored on the progress.jsonl `verdict` event: the grouped-verdict JSON when `grouped` is true, otherwise the same text as `global_verdict`. Kept so a consumer can reproduce the log byte for byte.

configuration.description: What produced the numbers. Mirrors the HTML report's configuration footer.

candidates.description: The configurations being compared, in declaration order. A 'candidate' is whatever the project varies — usually a model, sometimes a system prompt or a persona against a fixed model.

name.description: Unique label. This is the key used in `aggregate` and in each test case's `candidates` map.

provider.description: Backend that served the model, e.g. google, ollama, anthropic, openai.

disable_safety.description: Whether provider safety filters were switched off for this candidate.

thinking.description: Reasoning/thinking setting as written in candidates.json: a boolean, or a provider-specific string such as "default", "low", "high".

system_prompt_file.description: File under the project's system_prompts/ whose content was used as the system instruction, or null for a bare baseline. The resolved text itself is deliberately not included here.

repetitions.description: How many times each candidate answered each test case. The length of the `values` arrays below is this number times the number of test cases (pooled) or this number alone (per test case), minus anything an interrupted run never produced.

group_verdicts.description: Whether the verdict judge was asked for one verdict per group.

global_criteria.description: The project-wide criterion applied to every response, independently of each test case's own criteria.

mode.description: How the global score was produced. "none" means global scoring was off, and every global_score in this file is the -1 sentinel.

criteria.description: The criteria text the active mode used: a rubric for llm-judge, a target response for similarity, a Python lambda source for assert. Empty when mode is "none".

test_judge.description: The LLM that scored each response against its test case's criteria.

reasoning.description: The reasoning-analysis instrument. The taxonomy comes from the tool's root config.json rather than the project, so that profiles from different benchmarks are comparable.

enabled.description: Whether the analysis phase ran at all. Equivalent to scope != "none".

scope.description: Which traces were analysed. "best" measures only the highest-scoring repetition of each candidate x test case — the one this file reports under `best` — so its figures are not comparable with an "all" run's.

schema_stamp.description: Identifier of the taxonomy in force when this file was written, e.g. "framing+solving+presentation@1a2b3c4d". Compare it with the per-analysis `schema_stamp` values: if they differ, the file mixes analyses produced by different schema versions and they must not be averaged together.

intensity_scale.description: Upper bound of a unit's per-dimension score. Units are scored 0..intensity_scale on each dimension.

dimensions.description: The axes each trace unit is scored on. INDEPENDENT axes, not a partition: one sentence may score on several at once, so the coverages need not sum to 1 and their sum is reported separately as `density`.

name.description: Dimension key. The per-unit scores and the coverage_* fields use this name.

definition.description: The single-concept question the judge was asked for this dimension.

color.description: Display colour used by the HTML report, as #rrggbb.

judge.description: The LLM that scored the trace units.

dimension_mode.description: "split" asks one single-concept question per dimension, "joint" asks for all of them in one call. null means the project left it unset and the tool's default applied.

aggregate.description: One record per candidate, pooling every repetition of every test case — the report's STATS row. Keys are candidate names, matching configuration.candidates[].name.

combined_avg.description: Task and global score means averaged, or whichever of the two was actually measured. -1 when neither was. This is the headline figure the HTML shows next to each candidate's name.

test_cases.description: One entry per test case, in declaration order.

group.description: Grouping label. Drives the per-group verdicts when configuration.group_verdicts is true.

judge_type.description: How this test case's task score was produced. "llm-judge": an LLM scored the response against `criteria`. "similarity": cosine similarity between embeddings of the response and `criteria`, scaled to 1-10. "assert": `criteria` is a Python lambda evaluated against the response text, and its author controls the returned score directly — including a deliberate -1 for 'not applicable'.

prompt.description: The prompt sent to every candidate for this test case.

criteria.description: The evaluation criteria, read according to `judge_type`.

files_used.description: Attachments sent with the prompt, as paths relative to the project directory. Empty when the test case has none.

candidates.description: Per-candidate results for this test case. Keys are candidate names; a candidate with no recorded repetition for this test case is absent rather than present-and-empty.

best.description: The highest-scoring repetition of this candidate on this test case — the one the HTML report displays. The other repetitions' texts are not in this file; they are in progress.jsonl.

output.description: The response text. Empty when no repetition produced one.

reason.description: The task judge's justification for the score.

global_reason.description: The global judge's justification. Empty when global scoring is off.

reasoning_text.description: The thinking trace of this repetition, verbatim. Emitted in full because `reasoning_analysis.units` are character offsets into THIS string: without it they cannot be resolved. Empty when the model returned no trace. Whether it is the raw chain of thought or a provider-written summary is recorded in reasoning_analysis.reasoning_is_summary.

reasoning_analysis.description: The per-unit analysis of `reasoning_text`, or null when this trace was not analysed (analysis off, or scope "best" and this was not the best repetition).

statBlock.description: One measured quantity: its mean, its standard deviation, and every raw value behind them. -1 values in `values` are the 'not measured' sentinel and are EXCLUDED from mean and std rather than averaged in as low results — so `values` may be longer than the sample the mean describes, and a mean of -1 means nothing measurable was recorded at all.

mean.description: Mean of the measured values, or -1 when none were.

std.description: Population standard deviation of the measured values.

values.description: One entry per repetition, in the order they ran. This is the detail the HTML report does not show.

performance.description: The measured quantities of one candidate, either pooled over the whole run or for a single test case.

score.description: Task score, 1-10, per the test case's judge_type. -1 means the evaluator itself failed. An `assert` test case's author may also return -1 deliberately to mean 'not applicable to this response'.

global_score.description: Score against the project-wide global criteria, 1-10. All -1 when configuration.global_criteria.mode is "none".

tokens.description: Output tokens billed for the response.

reasoning_tokens.description: Thinking tokens billed. 0 for models that do not think, or that were run with thinking off.

time.description: Wall-clock seconds for the generation call. Per-process one-off costs (SDK import, client construction, attachment upload) are warmed up before the clock starts, so these are comparable across candidates within one run — but not across runs on different hardware or networks.

cost_per_point.description: Thinking tokens spent per point of task score; lower is cheaper. A DIAGNOSTIC, NOT A RANKING KEY: the score floors at 1 and spans only 10x while token counts span far more, so a candidate that thinks little and fails scores well here.

pooled.description: Ratio of the means: mean(reasoning_tokens) / mean(score). -1 when there is no thinking to price or no score to price it against.

mean.description: Mean of each repetition's OWN ratio — a different statistic from `pooled`, which it need not equal. The two diverge the more the score varies across the repetitions this record spans.

std.description: Standard deviation of the per-repetition ratios averaged in `mean`.

reasoningProfile.description: Reasoning figures pooled over every analysed repetition of one candidate. An EMPTY OBJECT when nothing was analysed. Keys are avg_<metric> and std_<metric> for each metric of reasoningAnalysis, plus the three below. A coverage of 0.0 is a real measurement — the trace really spent none of itself on that dimension — and must not be read as -1 'not measured'.

n.description: How many per-repetition analyses were pooled.

is_summary.description: True when ANY pooled trace was a provider-written summary rather than the raw chain of thought. When true, never compare this profile's length- or composition-derived figures against a raw-trace candidate's: they partly measure the summariser.

schema_stamps.description: The distinct taxonomy stamps behind the pooled analyses. More than one entry means the figures mix schema versions and should not be read as one measurement.

reasoningAnalysis.description: The analysis of one thinking trace. The trace is split PROCEDURALLY into sentence-sized units before any LLM sees it, so full coverage and zero overlap are structural; the judge only ever returns numbers against unit ids.

units.description: The trace's units in order, each a character span of best.reasoning_text.

end.description: Exclusive end offset into best.reasoning_text. Gaps between consecutive units are whitespace.

solving.description: This unit's solving intensity, on the same scale.

presentation.description: This unit's presentation intensity, on the same scale.

coverage_framing.description: Share of the trace, weighted by unit length, spent on framing. In [0,1], or -1 if not measured. 0.0 is a real measurement.

coverage_solving.description: Share spent on solving. In [0,1], or -1 if not measured. 0.0 is a real measurement.

coverage_presentation.description: Share spent on presentation. In [0,1], or -1 if not measured. 0.0 is a real measurement.

density.description: Sum of the three coverages: how many concerns the trace carries per unit of text. Exceeds 1 when units score on several dimensions at once. -1 if not measured.

alt_path.description: How many alternative approaches the trace weighed, counted as the number of units cited in alt_path_units. -1 if not measured.

autocorrect.description: How many times the trace corrected itself, counted as the number of units cited in autocorrect_units. -1 if not measured.

alignment_score.description: How well the final response follows what the trace concluded, 1-10. Below 8 the judge must cite the contradicted units in alignment_evidence. -1 if not measured.

alt_path_units.description: 1-based indices into `units` where an alternative was weighed.

autocorrect_units.description: 1-based indices into `units` where the trace corrected itself.

alignment_evidence.description: 1-based indices into `units` that the final response contradicts.

repetition_rate.description: How much of the trace restates itself, in [0,1]. Computed procedurally with no LLM call. 0.0 is a real measurement.

trace_response_drift.description: Textual similarity between the trace and the response, in [0,1]. Computed procedurally with no LLM call. Low values mean the response says something the trace did not.

reasoning_is_summary.description: True when the provider returned a summary the model wrote about its own reasoning rather than the raw chain of thought (Google does; the others do not). null for traces recorded before providers reported this — read null as 'unknown', never as 'raw'. Length and composition figures of a summarised trace must never be ranked against a raw one.

schema_stamp.description: The taxonomy version this analysis was produced under. Compare with configuration.reasoning.schema_stamp.
